docs.title: HiReS documentation
docs.text:
Version 2.0 · Source · Issues · Release notes

HiReS (High-Resolution Segmentation) is a Python library and command-line tool for instance segmentation and morphometric analysis of images that are too large for a single neural-network pass. It cuts a scan into overlapping tiles, runs a YOLO segmentation model on each tile, stitches the detections back into polygons in full-image coordinates, measures the shape of every object, and evaluates the result against ground truth.

import hires

collection = hires.segment("scan.tif", "DaphnAI.pt")
collection.with_scale(dpi=2400, unit="um").to_csv("traits.csv")

  • Getting started

    New to HiReS? Install it and segment your first image in a few minutes.

    Installation · Quickstart

  • User guide

    Background and worked explanations: the data model, the tiling algorithm, the trait definitions and the evaluation protocol.

    Open the user guide

  • API reference

    Every public class, function and constant, with parameters, return values and examples. Assumes you know the concepts.

    Open the reference

  • Command line

    The hires command: run, chunk, plot and evaluate, and the files they write.

    The hires command · Output files

docs.title: What HiReS does
docs.text: Tiled segmentation Images of 10,000 × 10,000 pixels and more are split into overlapping tiles so that inference runs on a laptop CPU or a single GPU. Objects cut by a tile border are dropped from that tile and recovered from its neighbour; duplicates are removed with polygon non-maximum suppression. See Tiled segmentation. A small, immutable data model Annotation (one polygon), Collection (one image) and Album (one dataset). Every operation returns a new object, so pipelines are chains of method calls with no hidden state. See The data model. Morphometric traits Area, perimeter, solidity, convexity, circularity and the dimensions of the axis-aligned and oriented bounding boxes, in pixels or in physical units derived from the scan resolution. See Morphometric traits. Evaluation against ground truth IoU matching, per-class precision, recall, F1 and average precision, confusion matrices, precision-recall curves and per-object comparison figures. See Evaluation. Model-agnostic Any Ultralytics YOLO segmentation model works, as does any object with a compatible predict() method. YOLO itself is an optional dependency: reading, measuring and evaluating label files needs no deep-learning stack.

docs.title: How the package is organised
docs.text:
HiReS is laid out like NumPy or SciPy. The objects you use every day live in the top-level namespace; specialised functionality lives in submodules.

Namespace Contents hires Data model, readers, segment, run_pipeline, measure, evaluate hires.metrics Matching predictions to ground truth and detection metrics hires.plot Overlays, comparison images and evaluation charts hires.tiling Splitting images and labels into tiles and merging them back hires.io Low-level image and label reading helpers hires.analysis Trait-agreement plots (legacy)

docs.title: Reporting bugs and requesting features
docs.text:
Open an issue. For a bug, include

  • what you did, as a minimal piece of code or the exact command,
  • what you expected and what happened instead, with the full traceback,
  • the output of hires.show_versions().

For a larger change, please open an issue before writing code, so the design can be discussed first.

docs.title: Code conventions
docs.text:
Style. Code is linted with Ruff, configured in pyproject.toml. The line length is 100.

Public API. A name is public if it is listed in the __all__ of its module and documented in the reference. Everyday objects are re-exported from hires/__init__.py; specialised ones stay in their submodule.

Design rules. These keep the package predictable; please follow them in new code.

  • Objects of the data model are immutable. Methods return new objects.
  • Sizes are (width, height), in pixels.
  • Functions comparing two sets of annotations take the ground truth first.
  • Everything after the essential arguments is keyword-only.
  • Heavy or optional dependencies (matplotlib, cv2, pandas, ultralytics) are imported inside the functions that need them, so that import hires stays fast. Optional ones go through hires.errors.require, which raises a MissingDependencyError naming the extra to install.
  • The library never prints and never configures logging. Use logging.getLogger(__name__) for progress and HiresWarning for results that are probably not what the user intended.
  • Plotting functions return what they drew, never call plt.show(), and accept save=.

Type hints are required for public functions. The package ships a py.typed marker.

docs.title: Docstrings
docs.text:
Docstrings follow the numpydoc standard and are enforced by Ruff's D rules. A public function documents its parameters, return value and raised exceptions, and should have an example:

def iou(a, b):
    """Intersection-over-union of two polygons.

    Parameters
    ----------
    a, b : Annotation or shapely.geometry.Polygon

    Returns
    -------
    float
        Value in ``[0, 1]``; ``0.0`` when the polygons do not overlap.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> from shapely.geometry import box
    >>> hires.metrics.iou(box(0, 0, 2, 1), box(1, 0, 3, 1))
    0.3333333333333333

Cross-references use reStructuredText roles, e.g. :func:`hires.measure` or :meth:`Collection.nms`; the extension in tools/griffe_rst.py turns them into links when the reference is built. Examples that need files or a model are marked # doctest: +SKIP.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
pytest                         # the whole suite
pytest tests/test_metrics.py   # one file
pytest -k nms                  # tests matching a keyword
  • Every bug fix comes with a test that fails without the fix.
  • Every new public function comes with tests of its behaviour and of its error cases.
  • Tests must not need network access, a GPU or model weights. Use the fixtures in tests/conftest.py: small synthetic images and FakeModel, a stand-in for an Ultralytics model.
  • A HiresWarning raised during a test is an error. A test that expects one must say so with pytest.warns.

docs.text:

docs.title: Examples with output
docs.text:
The user guide follows the NumPy and Shapely manuals: every feature is shown as an interactive example, the statement after >>> and its output below it.

  • Examples must run as they are, without a model or files of the reader. Build small objects in the page, or write the files the example needs.
  • Never type output by hand. Write the statements, then run make examples. tools/doc_examples.py executes each page from top to bottom in an empty directory and fills in what was printed. A PNG that a page saves and embeds as assets/examples/{name}.png is copied into docs/assets/examples/.
  • The pages are also tests: pytest runs them as doctests, so an example whose output changed fails CI.
  • Keep output portable: show path.name, not paths; round floats; wrap NumPy scalars in float().
  • Mark statements that need a real model or data # doctest: +SKIP.

A new public object needs a docstring and a hires.name entry on the matching page in docs/reference/; a new feature usually also deserves a paragraph in the user guide. make docs builds in strict mode and fails on broken links and unresolved cross-references.

docs.title: Pull requests
docs.text:
1. Create a branch from main.
  2. Make the change, with tests and documentation.
  3. Add an entry under Unreleased in CHANGELOG.md.
  4. Run make check and make docs.
  5. Open the pull request and describe what it changes and why.

Continuous integration runs the linter, the tests on every supported Python version, and the documentation build.

docs.title: Compatibility policy
docs.text:
HiReS follows semantic versioning.

  • The public API is everything documented in the reference, plus the options, output files and exit codes of the hires command.
  • Patch releases (2.0.x) fix bugs.
  • Minor releases (2.x.0) add features and may deprecate. A deprecated feature keeps working, emits a DeprecationWarning, and is removed no earlier than the next major release.
  • Major releases may break compatibility, with a migration guide.

Exceptions: hires.analysis is legacy code outside this policy, and numerical results may change in the last digits between releases.

Supported Python versions are those listed in pyproject.toml; support for a version is dropped only in a minor or major release.

docs.title: Releasing
docs.text:
For maintainers.

  1. Update version in pyproject.toml and CITATION.cff.
  2. In CHANGELOG.md, rename Unreleased to the version, add the date and the link at the bottom, and start a new empty Unreleased section.
  3. Run make check docs build.

  4. Commit, tag and push:

    git commit -am "Release 2.0.0"
git tag v2.0.0
git push origin main --tags

  5. Create a GitHub release from the tag. The Publish workflow builds the distributions and uploads them to PyPI; the Docs workflow deploys the documentation.

docs.title: Release notes
docs.text: All notable changes to HiReS are documented here. The format follows Keep a Changelog and the project adheres to Semantic Versioning.
A rewrite of the Python API around a small, immutable data model. The command line is largely unchanged. Code written against 1.x needs to be updated; see the migration guide.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• hires.metrics: IoU matching (match, MatchResult, Match), per-class detection_report with AP50 and AP50-95, confusion_matrix, precision_recall_curve and average_precision.
  • hires.evaluate and the hires evaluate command, which write a complete evaluation report to a directory.
  • hires.plot: overlay, comparison, individual, annotation, confusion_matrix, precision_recall and training_curves.
  • hires.tiling: tile_grid, iter_tiles, tile_image, tile_annotations, merge_tiles and parse_tile_name.
  • hires.segment, hires.Segmenter and hires.run_pipeline. Any object with a compatible predict() method can be used as the model.
  • hires.ClassMapping and hires.build_class_mapping for translating class ids between labelling schemas, including classes that were split.
  • Album.balance for reducing class imbalance in tiled training sets.
  • An exception hierarchy (HiresError, AnnotationFormatError, MissingDependencyError) and HiresWarning.
  • hires.show_versions for bug reports.
  • hires run --batch-size and hires --version.
  • Type hints throughout and a py.typed marker.
  • A test suite, and a documentation site with a user guide and a generated API reference.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Breaking: everything common is imported from the top-level hires namespace. The Settings dataclass and the SegmentationPipeline and PlottingPipeline classes are replaced by functions with keyword arguments.
  • Breaking: Annotation, Collection and Album are immutable. Methods that used to modify an object now return a new one.
  • Breaking: traits are computed on demand. The image size and physical scale belong to the Collection, not to each Annotation.
  • Breaking: ultralytics is an optional dependency (hireseg[yolo]). scipy, plotnine and SkillMetrics moved to hireseg[analysis].
  • Breaking: the layout of the {stem}_debug/ directory.
  • Progress is reported through the standard logging module instead of tqdm and print.
  • The hires command returns meaningful exit codes.

docs.title: Removed
docs.text:
• Breaking: the subpackages hires.models, hires.pipeline, hires.processing, hires.operations and hires.viz.
  • The tqdm dependency.

docs.title: Deprecated
docs.text: • hires.analysis is legacy code and will be removed or replaced in a future release.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: HiReS requires Python 3.10 or newer. The distribution is called hireseg; the import name and the command are hires.

docs.title: Install from PyPI
docs.text:
Segmentation and analysisAnalysis onlyEverything 
pip install "hireseg[yolo]"

Installs HiReS together with Ultralytics (and therefore PyTorch), which is needed to run a model.

pip install hireseg

Enough to read, measure, filter, plot and evaluate label files. No deep-learning stack is installed.

pip install "hireseg[all]"

docs.title: Optional dependencies
docs.text:
The core install is deliberately light. Features that need heavy packages are grouped in extras:

Extra Installs Needed for yolo ultralytics hires.segment, hires.Segmenter, hires.run_pipeline, hires run, and reading class names from .pt weights analysis scipy, plotnine, SkillMetrics The legacy trait-agreement plots in hires.analysis all yolo + analysis Everything above dev pytest, ruff Running the tests and the linter docs mkdocs-material, mkdocstrings[python] Building this documentation

docs.title: GPU support
docs.text:
HiReS runs on the CPU by default. To use a GPU, install a PyTorch build that matches your CUDA version before installing the yolo extra, following the selector on pytorch.org:

pip install torch torchvision --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu121
pip install "hireseg[yolo]"

Then pass device="0" (Python) or --device 0 (command line).

cd HiReS

docs.text:
hires --version

hires.show_versions()

docs.title: Migrating from 1.x
docs.text: HiReS 2.0 is a rewrite of the Python API. The command line is largely unchanged; Python code written against 1.x needs to be updated. This page maps the old names to the new ones.

docs.title: What changed, in short
docs.text:
• One flat namespace. Everything common is imported from hires directly. The subpackages hires.models, hires.pipeline, hires.processing, hires.operations and hires.viz are gone.
  • Functions instead of pipeline classes. The Settings dataclass and the SegmentationPipeline / PlottingPipeline classes are replaced by functions that take keyword arguments.
  • Immutable objects. Annotation, Collection and Album can no longer be modified in place. Methods that used to mutate now return a new object.
  • Traits are computed on demand. An annotation no longer carries its image size or scale; the collection does.
  • YOLO is optional. ultralytics moved to the yolo extra; scipy, plotnine and SkillMetrics moved to the analysis extra; tqdm is no longer used.
  • New: hires evaluate, hires.metrics, hires.plot, a dedicated exception hierarchy and standard-library logging.

docs.title: Running the pipeline
docs.text:
1.x2.0 
from hires.models import Settings
from hires.pipeline.seg_pipeline import SegmentationPipeline

cfg = Settings(
    source="data/images/",
    model_path="models/model.pt",
    output_dir="results/",
    conf=0.58,
    chunk_size=(1024, 1024),
    overlap=300,
    iou_thresh=0.7,
    save_crops=True,
)
SegmentationPipeline(cfg).run()

import hires

album = hires.run_pipeline(
    "data/images/",
    "models/model.pt",
    "results/",
    confidence=0.58,
    tile_size=(1024, 1024),
    overlap=300,
    nms_iou=0.7,
    save_crops=True,
)

The Python API now says tile where 1.x said chunk. The command line keeps the old spelling (hires chunk, --chunk-size).

docs.title: Measurements
docs.text:
In 1.x the traits were properties of the annotation. In 2.0 they are computed by Annotation.traits (or the stand-alone hires.measure) and returned as a dict:

1.x2.0 
ann.area
ann.circularity
width, length = ann.oriented_bounding_box.width_length

traits = ann.traits(collection.image_size, pixel_size=collection.pixel_size)
traits["area"]
traits["circularity"]
traits["obb_width"], traits["obb_length"]

In practice you rarely measure a single annotation; Collection.to_frame measures all of them with the right image size and scale.

docs.title: Tables
docs.text:
• The identifier column of trait tables is now name (1.x: collection_name).
  • The match table returned by MatchResult.to_frame uses the prefixes gt_ and pred_ (1.x pairs_df: left_ and right_).

docs.text: The layout of {stem}_debug/ changed; see Output files.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
hires run, hires chunk and hires plot accept the same options as before. New in 2.0:

  • hires evaluate compares predictions with ground truth.
  • hires run --batch-size sets the number of tiles per model call.
  • hires --version.
  • Exit codes are meaningful; see The hires command.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
This page is a short, hands-on tour of HiReS. Every example shows the commands as you would type them at the Python prompt (>>>) followed by what they print, and can be pasted into a Python session as it is.

>>> import hires

docs.title: Segment an image
docs.text:
With a high-resolution image and YOLO segmentation weights, hires.segment does the whole job: it cuts the image into overlapping tiles, runs the model on each tile, and merges the detections. This step needs the yolo extra (see Installation).

>>> collection = hires.segment("scan.tif", "DaphnAI.pt")  # doctest: +SKIP

The result is a Collection: the detected objects of one image. The same object is returned when you read a label file, which is what the rest of this page does, so that you can follow along without a model or an image.

docs.title: A collection without a model
docs.text:
HiReS stores detections in YOLO segmentation label files: one line per object, holding the class id, the polygon as x y pairs, and the confidence. Let us write a small one by hand, with four objects:

>>> from pathlib import Path
>>> labels = """\
... 0 0.10 0.10 0.30 0.10 0.30 0.30 0.10 0.30 0.95
... 0 0.50 0.20 0.70 0.20 0.70 0.35 0.50 0.35 0.88
... 1 0.20 0.60 0.28 0.60 0.28 0.90 0.20 0.90 0.71
... 1 0.60 0.60 0.62 0.60 0.62 0.63 0.60 0.63 0.35
... """
>>> _ = Path("scan.txt").write_text(labels)

and read it back. The coordinates in the file are fractions of the image width and height, so we also say how large the image is, as (width, height) in pixels:

>>> collection = hires.read_txt("scan.txt", image_size=(800, 400))
>>> collection
Collection(name='scan', n=4, image_size=(800, 400))

A collection behaves like a list of Annotation objects:

>>> len(collection)
4
>>> collection[0]
Annotation(class_id=0, confidence=0.950, vertices=4)
>>> collection.class_counts()
{0: 2, 1: 2}

docs.title: Measure
docs.text:
to_frame returns a pandas.DataFrame with one row per object and one column per morphometric trait:

>>> traits = collection.to_frame()
>>> traits[["class_id", "confidence", "area", "obb_length", "obb_width"]]
   class_id  confidence     area  obb_length  obb_width
0         0        0.95  12800.0       160.0       80.0
1         0        0.88   9600.0       160.0       60.0
2         1        0.71   7680.0       120.0       64.0
3         1        0.35    192.0        16.0       12.0

The values are in pixels, because the collection knows its image size but not the physical size of a pixel. Attach the scan resolution to measure in physical units instead:

>>> scaled = collection.with_scale(dpi=2400, unit="um")
>>> scaled.to_frame()[["class_id", "area", "obb_length", "obb_width"]].round(1)
   class_id       area  obb_length  obb_width
0         0  1433688.9      1693.3      846.7
1         0  1075266.7      1693.3      635.0
2         1   860213.3      1270.0      677.3
3         1    21505.3       169.3      127.0

Note that with_scale did not change collection. Collections are immutable: every method returns a new one.

All nine traits are defined in Morphometric traits.

docs.title: Filter
docs.text:
Methods can be chained. Here we keep confident detections, drop everything smaller than 10⁵ µm², and count what is left:

>>> animals = scaled.filter_confidence(0.5).filter_area(min_area=1e5)
>>> animals
Collection(name='scan', n=3, image_size=(800, 400), dpi=2400, unit='um')
>>> animals.class_counts()
{0: 2, 1: 1}

More in Filtering and class handling.

docs.title: Plot
docs.text:
hires.plot.overlay draws a collection on its image. We have no image here, so we draw on an empty grey canvas of the right size:

>>> import numpy as np
>>> canvas = np.full((400, 800, 3), 70, dtype=np.uint8)
>>> rgb = hires.plot.overlay(
...     canvas, collection, class_names={0: "pulex", 1: "galeata"},
...     save="quickstart_overlay.png",
... )
>>> rgb.shape
(400, 800, 3)

The number in front of each label is the position of the object in the collection: the object labelled 2 is collection[2]. With a real scan, pass its path instead of canvas.

docs.title: Evaluate against ground truth
docs.text:
Suppose a person annotated the same image and found three objects. Ground truth has no confidence, so each line ends after the last coordinate:

>>> manual = """\
... 0 0.10 0.10 0.30 0.10 0.30 0.30 0.10 0.30
... 0 0.50 0.20 0.70 0.20 0.70 0.36 0.50 0.36
... 0 0.20 0.60 0.28 0.60 0.28 0.90 0.20 0.90
... """
>>> _ = Path("scan_gt.txt").write_text(manual)
>>> gt = hires.read_txt("scan_gt.txt", image_size=(800, 400))

hires.metrics.match pairs each prediction with the ground-truth object it overlaps. The ground truth always comes first:

>>> matches = hires.metrics.match(gt, collection)
>>> matches.counts()
{'tp': 2, 'misclassified': 1, 'fp': 1, 'fn': 0}

Two objects were found with the right class (tp), one was found but given the wrong class (misclassified), and one prediction has no counterpart (fp). The table behind these numbers:

>>> matches.to_frame()[["status", "iou", "gt_class", "pred_class", "pred_confidence"]]
          status     iou  gt_class  pred_class  pred_confidence
0             tp  1.0000         0           0             0.95
1  misclassified  1.0000         0           1             0.71
2             tp  0.9375         0           0             0.88
3             fp  0.0000      <NA>           1             0.35

and the usual summary metrics per class:

>>> report = hires.metrics.detection_report(gt, collection)
>>> report[["tp", "fp", "fn", "precision", "recall", "f1"]].round(2)
          tp  fp  fn  precision  recall    f1
class_id
all        2   2   1        0.5    0.67  0.57
0          2   0   1        1.0    0.67  0.80
1          0   2   0        0.0    0.00  0.00

Evaluation explains the matching and every metric.

docs.title: Whole directories, and the command line
docs.text:
For a directory of scans, hires.run_pipeline segments every image and writes labels, trait tables and overlays; hires.read_album reads a directory of label files back as an Album, a named set of collections; and hires.evaluate writes a complete evaluation report.

>>> album = hires.run_pipeline(  # doctest: +SKIP
...     "scans/", "DaphnAI.pt", "results/", dpi=2400, unit="um"
... )
>>> gt = hires.read_album("labels/", image_dir="scans/")  # doctest: +SKIP
>>> report = hires.evaluate(gt, album, "evaluation/")  # doctest: +SKIP

The same three steps from a terminal:

hires run -s scans/ -m DaphnAI.pt -o results/ --dpi 2400 --unit um
hires evaluate --gt labels/ --pred results/ --images scans/ -o evaluation/

The files this produces are listed in Output files.

def show_versions() -> None:
    """Print the versions of HiReS and its dependencies.

    Include the output when reporting a bug.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> hires.show_versions()  # doctest: +SKIP
    hireseg      : 2.0.0
    python       : 3.12.3
    ...
    """
    import platform

    rows = [
        ("hireseg", __version__),
        ("python", platform.python_version()),
        ("platform", platform.platform()),
    ]
    for module in (
        "numpy", "pandas", "shapely", "PIL", "cv2", "matplotlib", "yaml", "ultralytics", "torch",
    ):  # fmt: skip
        try:
            found = getattr(importlib.import_module(module), "__version__", "unknown")
        except ImportError:
            found = "not installed"
        rows.append((module, found))
    for name, value in rows:
        print(f"{name:<12} : {value}")

def __init__(
    self,
    collections: Iterable[Collection] = (),
    *,
    name: str | None = None,
) -> None:
    seen: Counter[str] = Counter()
    unique: list[Collection] = []
    renamed: list[tuple[str, str]] = []

    for collection in collections:
        if not isinstance(collection, Collection):
            raise TypeError(
                f"Album items must be Collection objects, got {type(collection).__name__}."
            )
        if not collection.name:
            raise ValueError("Every collection in an Album needs a non-empty name.")
        original = collection.name
        if seen[original]:
            new_name = f"{original}__{seen[original]}"
            collection = collection.replace(name=new_name)
            renamed.append((original, new_name))
        seen[original] += 1
        unique.append(collection)

    if renamed:
        warnings.warn(
            f"{len(renamed)} collection(s) with duplicate names were renamed "
            f"(e.g. {renamed[0][0]!r} -> {renamed[0][1]!r}).",
            HiresWarning,
            stacklevel=2,
        )

    self._collections = tuple(unique)
    self._by_name = {c.name: c for c in self._collections}
    self._name = None if name is None else str(name)

A collection is majority-only when all of its annotations belong to majority_classes (empty collections count too). Such collections are removed in random order until:

def balance(
    self,
    majority_classes: Iterable[int],
    *,
    max_ratio: float = 3.0,
    seed: int | None = 42,
) -> Album:
    """Drop majority-only collections to reduce class imbalance.

    A collection is *majority-only* when all of its annotations belong to
    ``majority_classes`` (empty collections count too). Such collections
    are removed in random order until::

        n_majority_annotations <= max_ratio * n_minority_annotations

    Collections containing any minority annotation are always kept.

    Parameters
    ----------
    majority_classes : iterable of int
        Over-represented class ids.
    max_ratio : float, default 3.0
        Largest accepted majority-to-minority annotation ratio.
    seed : int or None, default 42
        Seed for the random selection and the final shuffle.

    Returns
    -------
    Album
        The balanced album, in shuffled order.
    """
    majority = set(majority_classes)
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    def n_majority(collection: Collection) -> int:
        return sum(a.class_id in majority for a in collection)

    majority_only = [c for c in self._collections if n_majority(c) == len(c)]
    mixed = [c for c in self._collections if n_majority(c) != len(c)]

    n_minority = sum(len(c) - n_majority(c) for c in mixed)
    budget = int(max_ratio * n_minority)
    running = sum(n_majority(c) for c in mixed)

    rng.shuffle(majority_only)
    kept = []
    for collection in majority_only:
        count = n_majority(collection)
        if running + count <= budget:
            kept.append(collection)
            running += count

    balanced = mixed + kept
    rng.shuffle(balanced)
    return Album(balanced, name=self._name)

def to_records(self) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Return one flat dict per annotation across all collections.

    Same fields as :meth:`Collection.to_records` plus ``album``.
    """
    records = []
    missing = 0
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore", HiresWarning)
        for collection in self._collections:
            missing += collection.image_size is None and len(collection) > 0
            for row in collection.to_records():
                records.append({"album": self._name, **row})
    if missing:
        warnings.warn(
            f"{missing} collection(s) have no image_size; their traits are "
            "measured in normalized coordinates. Load the album with "
            "image_dir=... to measure in pixels.",
            HiresWarning,
            stacklevel=2,
        )
    return records

def to_frame(self) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return every annotation and its traits as a ``pandas.DataFrame``.

    Same columns as :meth:`Collection.to_frame`, preceded by ``album``.
    """
    import pandas as pd

    from .annotation import TRAIT_NAMES

    columns = [
        "album",
        "name",
        "image_path",
        "image_width",
        "image_height",
        "dpi",
        "unit",
        "class_id",
        "confidence",
        *TRAIT_NAMES,
    ]
    with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught:
        warnings.simplefilter("always", HiresWarning)
        records = self.to_records()
    for warning in caught:
        warnings.warn(warning.message, warning.category, stacklevel=2)
    return pd.DataFrame(records, columns=columns)

        closer than ``margin`` to any image edge is not within the frame.

    >>> Annotation(0, box(0.0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.4)).within_frame(0.01)
    False
    """

        self.polygon

def build_class_mapping(
    old_names: Mapping[int, str],
    new_names: Mapping[int, str],
    name_map: Mapping[str, str | Sequence[str]],
) -> ClassMapping:
    """Build a :class:`ClassMapping` between two class-name schemas.

    Parameters
    ----------
    old_names : mapping of int to str
        ``{old_id: old_label}`` of the schema the annotations currently use.
    new_names : mapping of int to str
        ``{new_id: new_label}`` of the target schema.
    name_map : mapping of str to (str or sequence of str)
        ``{old_label: new_label}`` for a direct rename, or
        ``{old_label: [candidate_new_labels]}`` for a class that is split in
        the new schema. Ambiguous entries are resolved per call to
        ``remap_classes``.

    Returns
    -------
    ClassMapping

    Raises
    ------
    KeyError
        If an old label has no entry in ``name_map`` or a target label does
        not exist in ``new_names``.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> mapping = build_class_mapping(
    ...     old_names={0: "ballooned", 1: "Daphnia"},
    ...     new_names={0: "d_pulex", 1: "d_galeata", 2: "ballooned"},
    ...     name_map={"ballooned": "ballooned", "Daphnia": ["d_pulex", "d_galeata"]},
    ... )
    >>> mapping.flatten({"Daphnia": "d_galeata"})
    {0: 2, 1: 1}
    """
    new_ids = {label: id_ for id_, label in new_names.items()}

    def lookup(label: str) -> int:
        if label not in new_ids:
            raise KeyError(f"Target label {label!r} not found in new_names.")
        return new_ids[label]

    mapping: dict[int, int | tuple[int, ...]] = {}
    for old_id, old_label in old_names.items():
        if old_label not in name_map:
            raise KeyError(f"name_map has no entry for old label {old_label!r}.")
        target = name_map[old_label]
        if isinstance(target, str):
            mapping[old_id] = lookup(target)
        else:
            mapping[old_id] = tuple(lookup(label) for label in target)

    return ClassMapping(mapping=mapping, old_names=dict(old_names), new_names=dict(new_names))

def flatten(self, resolve: Mapping[str, str] | None = None) -> dict[int, int]:
    """Resolve ambiguous entries and return a flat ``{old_id: new_id}`` dict.

    Parameters
    ----------
    resolve : mapping of str to str, optional
        ``{old_label: chosen_new_label}``. Required for every ambiguous
        entry.

    Raises
    ------
    KeyError
        If an ambiguous label is missing from ``resolve`` or the chosen
        label does not exist in the new schema.
    ValueError
        If the chosen label is not one of the declared candidates.
    """
    resolve = resolve or {}
    new_ids = {label: id_ for id_, label in self.new_names.items()}
    flat: dict[int, int] = {}

    for old_id, target in self.mapping.items():
        if isinstance(target, int):
            flat[old_id] = target
            continue

        old_label = self.old_names[old_id]
        candidates = [self.new_names[t] for t in target]
        if old_label not in resolve:
            raise KeyError(
                f"{old_label!r} is ambiguous {candidates}; choose one with resolve."
            )
        chosen = resolve[old_label]
        if chosen not in new_ids:
            raise KeyError(f"{chosen!r} is not a label of the new schema.")
        if new_ids[chosen] not in target:
            raise ValueError(
                f"resolve[{old_label!r}] = {chosen!r} is not among the "
                f"declared candidates {candidates}."
            )
        flat[old_id] = new_ids[chosen]

    return flat

docs.title: The hires command
docs.text:
Installing HiReS adds the hires command. It exposes the most common workflows without writing Python.

hires [--version] [--help] COMMAND [options]
Command Purpose Python equivalent hires run Segment images and write labels, tables and overlays hires.run_pipeline hires chunk Cut images into overlapping tiles hires.tiling.tile_image hires plot Draw existing label files on their images hires.plot.overlay hires evaluate Compare predictions with ground truth hires.evaluate

hires COMMAND --help prints the options of a command with their defaults and is always authoritative for the installed version.

Terminology

The command line speaks of chunks and the Python API of tiles. They are the same thing; the option names are kept from HiReS 1.x.

docs.title: hires run
docs.text:
Run the full pipeline on one image or on every image in a directory: tile → predict → filter edges → merge → NMS → write outputs. Needs the yolo extra.

hires run -s scans/ -m DaphnAI.pt -o results/ --dpi 2400 --unit um
Option Default Description -s, --source PATH required Image file or directory -m, --model PATH models/DaphnAI.pt YOLO segmentation weights -o, --output DIR results Root output directory -r, --recursive off Search the source directory recursively; the sub-directory layout is mirrored in the output --conf FLOAT 0.5 Minimum detection confidence --imgsz INT 1024 Size the model resizes each chunk to --device STR cpu Inference device: cpu, 0, cuda:0, … --batch-size INT 8 Chunks per model call --chunk-size W H 1024 1024 Chunk width and height in pixels --overlap INT 150 Pixels shared by adjacent chunks --edge-threshold FLOAT 0.01 Detections closer than this fraction of a chunk to its border are discarded --iou-thresh FLOAT 0.7 Polygon IoU above which the less confident of two detections is removed --save-crops off Write a masked crop of every detection --dpi FLOAT none Scan resolution; with --unit, traits are written in physical units --unit UNIT none nm, um, mm, cm, m or inch; requires --dpi --debug off Write intermediate files

An image that fails is logged and skipped; the remaining images are still processed. The meaning of the tiling and inference options is explained in Tiled segmentation; the files written are listed in Output files.

docs.title: hires chunk
docs.text:
Cut one image, or every image in a directory, into overlapping PNG tiles named {stem}_{x}_{y}.png.

hires chunk -s scans/ -o chunks/ --chunk-size 1024 1024 --overlap 150
Option Default Description -s, --source PATH required Image file or directory -o, --output DIR chunks Output directory -r, --recursive off Search the source directory recursively --chunk-size W H 1024 1024 Chunk width and height in pixels --overlap INT 150 Pixels shared by adjacent chunks

To tile the labels of an annotated image as well, use hires.tiling.tile_annotations from Python; see Tiling training data.

docs.title: hires plot
docs.text:
Draw existing YOLO-format label files on their images and write {stem}_annotated.png to the output directory.

hires plot -s scans/ --ann labels/ -o plots/ -m data.yaml
Option Default Description -s, --source PATH required Image file or directory --ann PATH the output directory A .txt file, or a directory of .txt files matched to images by file stem -m, --model PATH models/DaphnAI.pt Model weights (.pt) or a data YAML file; read for class names only -o, --output DIR results Output directory -r, --recursive off Search the source directory recursively

Without --ann, the label file of each image is expected at {output}/{stem}.txt, which is where hires run writes it.

docs.title: hires evaluate
docs.text:
Compare a directory of predicted label files with a directory of ground-truth label files. Files are paired by name. The per-class detection report is printed and the full report is written to the output directory.

hires evaluate --gt labels/ --pred results/ --images scans/ -n data.yaml
Option Default Description --gt DIR required Directory of ground-truth .txt files --pred DIR required Directory of predicted .txt files, e.g. the output of hires run --images DIR none Directory of the images; enables measurements in pixels and comparison images -n, --names PATH none Model weights (.pt) or a data YAML file; read for class names only -o, --output DIR evaluation Output directory --iou FLOAT 0.5 Minimum IoU for a prediction to match a ground-truth object --no-images off Do not write comparison images

Label files present on only one side are skipped with a warning. The metrics are defined in Evaluation; the files written are listed in Output files.

docs.text: Code Meaning 0 Success 1 Partial success: hires run skipped at least one image that failed, or hires plot found no label file for at least one image 2 Error: invalid arguments, a missing file or directory, nothing to process, or a missing optional dependency

def __init__(
    self,
    annotations: Iterable[Annotation] = (),
    *,
    name: str | None = None,
    image_path: str | os.PathLike[str] | None = None,
    image_size: tuple[int, int] | None = None,
    dpi: float | None = None,
    unit: str | None = None,
) -> None:
    items = tuple(annotations)
    for item in items:
        if not isinstance(item, Annotation):
            raise TypeError(
                f"Collection items must be Annotation objects, got {type(item).__name__}."
            )
    if (dpi is None) != (unit is None):
        raise ValueError("dpi and unit must be given together.")
    if unit is not None:
        pixel_size_from_dpi(dpi, unit)  # validates both
        if image_size is None:
            raise ValueError(
                "image_size is required to measure in physical units; "
                "pass image_size=(width, height) or load with an image."
            )
    if image_size is not None:
        width, height = image_size
        if not (width > 0 and height > 0):
            raise ValueError(f"image_size must be positive, got {image_size!r}.")
        image_size = (int(width), int(height))

    self._annotations = items
    self._name = None if name is None else str(name)
    self._image_path = None if image_path is None else Path(image_path)
    self._image_size = image_size
    self._dpi = None if dpi is None else float(dpi)
    self._unit = unit

def filter_area(
    self, min_area: float | None = None, max_area: float | None = None
) -> Collection:
    """Return the annotations whose area lies in ``[min_area, max_area]``.

    Removes debris (too small) and clumps (too large). Areas are in the
    units of :meth:`to_frame`: square pixels, or square physical units
    after :meth:`with_scale`; normalized when the image size is unknown.

    Parameters
    ----------
    min_area, max_area : float, optional
        Inclusive bounds; ``None`` leaves that side open.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> scaled = collection.with_scale(dpi=2400, unit="um")  # doctest: +SKIP
    >>> animals = scaled.filter_area(min_area=5e4)  # doctest: +SKIP
    """
    if min_area is not None and max_area is not None and min_area > max_area:
        raise ValueError("min_area must not exceed max_area.")
    scale = self.pixel_size**2
    if self._image_size is not None:
        scale *= self._image_size[0] * self._image_size[1]
    low = -math.inf if min_area is None else min_area
    high = math.inf if max_area is None else max_area
    return self.filter(lambda a: low <= a.polygon.area * scale <= high)

            for a in self._annotations

def nms(self, iou_threshold: float = 0.5, *, class_aware: bool = False) -> Collection:
    """Apply polygon non-maximum suppression.

    Annotations are visited in order of decreasing confidence (ties are
    broken in favour of the larger polygon). Each visited annotation
    suppresses every remaining annotation whose polygon IoU with it
    exceeds ``iou_threshold``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    iou_threshold : float, default 0.5
        Annotations overlapping a kept annotation by more than this IoU
        are removed.
    class_aware : bool, default False
        If true, only annotations of the same class suppress each other.

    Returns
    -------
    Collection
        The kept annotations, ordered by decreasing confidence.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If any annotation has no confidence, or the threshold is outside
        ``[0, 1]``.
    """
    from shapely.strtree import STRtree

    from .metrics import iou

    if not 0.0 <= iou_threshold <= 1.0:
        raise ValueError("iou_threshold must be between 0 and 1.")
    if any(a.confidence is None for a in self._annotations):
        raise ValueError("All annotations need a confidence for NMS.")
    if not self._annotations:
        return self

    ordered = sorted(
        self._annotations,
        key=lambda a: (a.confidence, a.polygon.area),
        reverse=True,
    )
    tree = STRtree([a.polygon for a in ordered])
    suppressed: set[int] = set()
    kept: list[Annotation] = []

    for i, annotation in enumerate(ordered):
        if i in suppressed:
            continue
        kept.append(annotation)
        for j in tree.query(annotation.polygon):
            j = int(j)
            if j <= i or j in suppressed:
                continue
            other = ordered[j]
            if class_aware and other.class_id != annotation.class_id:
                continue
            if iou(annotation, other) > iou_threshold:
                suppressed.add(j)

    return self.replace(annotations=kept)

def to_records(self) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Return one flat dict per annotation, including morphometric traits.

    Traits are measured in pixels when :attr:`image_size` is known, and
    in physical units when a scale is set with :meth:`with_scale`.
    Without an image size they are measured on the normalized polygons
    and a :class:`~hires.HiresWarning` is emitted.
    """
    if self._image_size is None and self._annotations:
        warnings.warn(
            f"Collection {self._name!r} has no image_size; traits are measured "
            "in normalized coordinates. Load it with an image to measure in pixels.",
            HiresWarning,
            stacklevel=2,
        )
    base = {
        "name": self._name,
        "image_path": None if self._image_path is None else str(self._image_path),
        "image_width": None if self._image_size is None else self._image_size[0],
        "image_height": None if self._image_size is None else self._image_size[1],
        "dpi": self._dpi,
        "unit": self._unit,
    }
    pixel_size = self.pixel_size
    return [
        {
            **base,
            "class_id": a.class_id,
            "confidence": a.confidence,
            **a.traits(self._image_size, pixel_size=pixel_size),
        }
        for a in self._annotations
    ]

def to_txt(self, path: str | os.PathLike[str], *, confidence: bool = True) -> None:
    """Write the collection as a YOLO segmentation label file.

    Each line is ``class_id x1 y1 x2 y2 ... xn yn [confidence]`` with
    normalized coordinates. Only polygon exteriors are written; interior
    holes cannot be represented in this format.

    Parameters
    ----------
    path : path-like
        Destination file; parent directories are created.
    confidence : bool, default True
        Append the confidence to each line when the annotation has one.
    """
    path = Path(path)
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    lines = []
    for a in self._annotations:
        coords = list(a.polygon.exterior.coords)[:-1]
        line = f"{a.class_id} " + " ".join(f"{x:.6f} {y:.6f}" for x, y in coords)
        if confidence and a.confidence is not None:
            line += f" {a.confidence:.6f}"
        lines.append(line)
    path.write_text("".join(line + "\n" for line in lines), encoding="utf-8")

def save_crops(
    self,
    directory: str | os.PathLike[str],
    *,
    mask: bool = True,
    padding: int = 0,
    prefix: str | None = None,
    format: str = "png",
) -> list[Path]:
    """Save one cropped image per annotation.

    Parameters
    ----------
    directory : path-like
        Output directory; created if needed.
    mask : bool, default True
        Black out the pixels outside the polygon.
    padding : int, default 0
        Extra pixels added around each bounding box.
    prefix : str, optional
        File name prefix. Defaults to the collection name.
    format : str, default "png"
        Image file extension understood by OpenCV.

    Returns
    -------
    list of pathlib.Path
        The written files, named ``{prefix}_{index:04d}_class_{class_id}``.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the collection has no ``image_path``.
    """
    import cv2
    import numpy as np

    from .io import read_image

    if self._image_path is None:
        raise ValueError("The collection has no image_path; use with_image() first.")
    image = read_image(self._image_path)
    height, width = image.shape[:2]

    directory = Path(directory)
    directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    prefix = prefix or self._name or "crop"
    extension = format.lstrip(".")
    saved: list[Path] = []

    for index, annotation in enumerate(self._annotations):
        polygon = annotation.to_pixels((width, height))
        min_x, min_y, max_x, max_y = polygon.bounds
        x0 = max(0, math.floor(min_x) - padding)
        y0 = max(0, math.floor(min_y) - padding)
        x1 = min(width, math.ceil(max_x) + padding)
        y1 = min(height, math.ceil(max_y) + padding)
        if x0 >= x1 or y0 >= y1:
            continue

        crop = image[y0:y1, x0:x1].copy()
        if mask:
            points = np.asarray(polygon.exterior.coords, dtype=np.float64)
            points -= (x0, y0)
            stencil = np.zeros(crop.shape[:2], dtype=np.uint8)
            cv2.fillPoly(stencil, [np.round(points).astype(np.int32)], 255)
            crop[stencil == 0] = 0

        path = directory / f"{prefix}_{index:04d}_class_{annotation.class_id}.{extension}"
        if not cv2.imwrite(str(path), crop):
            raise OSError(f"Could not write crop to {path}.")
        saved.append(path)

    return saved

def read_txt(
    path: str | os.PathLike[str],
    *,
    name: str | None = None,
    image: str | os.PathLike[str] | None = None,
    image_size: tuple[int, int] | None = None,
    on_error: OnError = "warn",
) -> Collection:
    """Read a YOLO segmentation label file into a :class:`~hires.Collection`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    path : path-like
        Label file with one ``class_id x1 y1 ... xn yn [confidence]`` line per
        object, in normalized coordinates.
    name : str, optional
        Name of the collection. Defaults to the file stem.
    image : path-like, optional
        Image the labels belong to. Its size is read from disk so that
        traits can be measured in pixels.
    image_size : tuple of int, optional
        ``(width, height)`` in pixels, as an alternative to ``image``.
    on_error : {"warn", "raise", "ignore"}, default "warn"
        What to do with lines that cannot be parsed (wrong token count,
        non-numeric values, degenerate polygons): skip them with a
        :class:`~hires.HiresWarning`, raise
        :class:`~hires.AnnotationFormatError`, or skip them silently.

    Returns
    -------
    Collection

    Raises
    ------
    FileNotFoundError
        If ``path`` or ``image`` does not exist.

    See Also
    --------
    read_album : Read a whole directory of label files.
    Collection.to_txt : Write a label file.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> collection = hires.read_txt("labels/scan.txt", image="images/scan.tif")  # doctest: +SKIP
    >>> collection.to_frame()[["class_id", "area"]]  # doctest: +SKIP
    """
    path = Path(path)
    if not path.is_file():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Annotation file not found: {path}")
    if on_error not in ("warn", "raise", "ignore"):
        raise ValueError("on_error must be 'warn', 'raise' or 'ignore'.")

    annotations: list[Annotation] = []
    problems: list[str] = []
    with path.open(encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        for number, line in enumerate(handle, start=1):
            if not line.strip():
                continue
            try:
                annotations.append(parse_line(line))
            except AnnotationFormatError as exc:
                message = f"{path}:{number}: {exc}"
                if on_error == "raise":
                    raise AnnotationFormatError(message) from None
                problems.append(message)

    if problems and on_error == "warn":
        warnings.warn(
            f"Skipped {len(problems)} unreadable line(s) in {path.name} "
            f"(first: {problems[0]}).",
            HiresWarning,
            stacklevel=2,
        )

    if image is not None and image_size is None:
        image_size = read_image_size(image)

    return Collection(
        annotations,
        name=name or path.stem,
        image_path=image,
        image_size=image_size,
    )

def read_album(
    source: str | os.PathLike[str] | Iterable[str | os.PathLike[str]],
    *,
    image_dir: str | os.PathLike[str] | None = None,
    name: str | None = None,
    image_extensions: Sequence[str] = IMAGE_EXTENSIONS,
    on_error: OnError = "warn",
) -> Album:
    """Read many YOLO label files into an :class:`~hires.Album`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    source : path-like or iterable of path-like
        A directory containing ``*.txt`` label files, or an explicit list of
        label files.
    image_dir : path-like, optional
        Directory with the images. Each label file ``{stem}.txt`` is bound to
        ``{image_dir}/{stem}{ext}`` when such a file exists.
    name : str, optional
        Name of the album. Defaults to the directory name.
    image_extensions : sequence of str, default :data:`IMAGE_EXTENSIONS`
        Extensions tried, in order, when looking for an image.
    on_error : {"warn", "raise", "ignore"}, default "warn"
        Handling of unreadable lines; see :func:`read_txt`.

    Returns
    -------
    Album
        One collection per label file, named after the file stem and sorted
        by file name when ``source`` is a directory.

    Raises
    ------
    FileNotFoundError
        If ``source`` or ``image_dir`` does not exist.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> gt = hires.read_album("labels/", image_dir="images/")  # doctest: +SKIP
    >>> gt.with_scale(dpi=2400, unit="um").to_csv("traits.csv")  # doctest: +SKIP
    """
    if isinstance(source, (str, os.PathLike)):
        directory = Path(source)
        if not directory.is_dir():
            raise FileNotFoundError(f"Annotation directory not found: {directory}")
        paths = sorted(directory.glob("*.txt"))
        name = name or directory.name
    else:
        paths = [Path(p) for p in source]

    if image_dir is not None:
        image_dir = Path(image_dir)
        if not image_dir.is_dir():
            raise FileNotFoundError(f"Image directory not found: {image_dir}")

    collections = []
    for path in paths:
        image = None
        if image_dir is not None:
            candidates = (image_dir / f"{path.stem}{ext}" for ext in image_extensions)
            image = next((c for c in candidates if c.is_file()), None)
        with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught:
            warnings.simplefilter("always", HiresWarning)
            collections.append(read_txt(path, image=image, on_error=on_error))
        for warning in caught:
            warnings.warn(warning.message, warning.category, stacklevel=2)

    return Album(collections, name=name)

    Parameters
    ----------

        ``.pt`` model file. Reading weights needs the ``yolo`` extra.

    Raises
    ------
    FileNotFoundError
        If ``path`` does not exist.
    KeyError
        If a YAML file has no ``names`` entry.
    """
    path = Path(path)
    if not path.is_file():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Class-name source not found: {path}")

    if path.suffix.lower() in {".yaml", ".yml"}:
        import yaml

        with path.open(encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            data = yaml.safe_load(handle) or {}
        if "names" not in data:
            raise KeyError(f"No 'names' entry in {path}.")
        names = data["names"]
    else:
        ultralytics = require("ultralytics", extra="yolo", feature="Reading model weights")
        names = ultralytics.YOLO(str(path)).names

    return normalize_class_names(names)

def find_images(
    source: str | os.PathLike[str],
    *,
    recursive: bool = False,
    extensions: Sequence[str] = IMAGE_EXTENSIONS,
) -> list[Path]:
    """List the image files at ``source``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    source : path-like
        An image file or a directory.
    recursive : bool, default False
        Descend into subdirectories.
    extensions : sequence of str, default :data:`IMAGE_EXTENSIONS`
        Accepted file extensions, case-insensitive.

    Returns
    -------
    list of pathlib.Path
        Sorted image paths; empty if ``source`` is a non-image file.

    Raises
    ------
    FileNotFoundError
        If ``source`` does not exist.
    """
    source = Path(source)
    allowed = {e.lower() for e in extensions}
    if source.is_file():
        return [source] if source.suffix.lower() in allowed else []
    if source.is_dir():
        pattern = "**/*" if recursive else "*"
        return sorted(
            p for p in source.glob(pattern) if p.is_file() and p.suffix.lower() in allowed
        )
    raise FileNotFoundError(f"No such file or directory: {source}")

def read_image_size(path: str | os.PathLike[str]) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """Return ``(width, height)`` of an image without decoding its pixels.

    Works for scans larger than Pillow's decompression-bomb limit.

    Raises
    ------
    FileNotFoundError
        If ``path`` does not exist.
    """
    from PIL import Image

    path = Path(path)
    if not path.is_file():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Image not found: {path}")
    # High-resolution scans routinely exceed PIL's bomb guard; lift it only

        Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS = None
        try:
            with Image.open(path) as image:
                return image.size
        finally:
            Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS = limit

def measure(polygon: Polygon, *, pixel_size: float = 1.0) -> dict[str, float]:
    """Measure the morphometric traits of a polygon.

    Parameters
    ----------
    polygon : shapely.geometry.Polygon
        Polygon in the coordinate system the measurements should be taken in
        (normally pixels).
    pixel_size : float, default 1.0
        Length of one coordinate unit in physical units. Lengths are
        multiplied by ``pixel_size`` and areas by ``pixel_size ** 2``.

    Returns
    -------
    dict of str to float
        One entry per name in :data:`TRAIT_NAMES`:

        ``area``, ``perimeter``
            Polygon area and exterior + interior boundary length.
        ``solidity``
            ``area / convex_hull_area``.
        ``convexity``
            ``convex_hull_perimeter / perimeter``.
        ``circularity``
            ``4 * pi * area / perimeter ** 2`` (1.0 for a circle).
        ``bbox_width``, ``bbox_height``
            Extent of the axis-aligned bounding box.
        ``obb_width``, ``obb_length``
            Short and long side of the minimum rotated bounding rectangle.

    Notes
    -----
    The shape ratios ``solidity``, ``convexity`` and ``circularity`` are
    dimensionless, but ``convexity`` and ``circularity`` are only meaningful
    when both axes share the same scale. Measure in pixel coordinates, not in
    normalized coordinates of a non-square image.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> from shapely.geometry import box
    >>> traits = measure(box(0, 0, 4, 2))
    >>> traits["area"], traits["obb_length"], traits["obb_width"]
    (8.0, 4.0, 2.0)
    """
    scale = float(pixel_size)
    area = polygon.area
    perimeter = polygon.length
    hull = polygon.convex_hull
    minx, miny, maxx, maxy = polygon.bounds
    obb_width, obb_length = _obb_sides(polygon)

    return {
        "area": area * scale**2,
        "perimeter": perimeter * scale,
        "solidity": area / hull.area if hull.area > 0 else 0.0,
        "convexity": hull.length / perimeter if perimeter > 0 else 0.0,
        "circularity": 4.0 * math.pi * area / perimeter**2 if perimeter > 0 else 0.0,
        "bbox_width": (maxx - minx) * scale,
        "bbox_height": (maxy - miny) * scale,
        "obb_width": obb_width * scale,
        "obb_length": obb_length * scale,
    }

def evaluate(
    gt: Collection | Album,
    pred: Collection | Album,
    output_dir: str | os.PathLike[str],
    *,
    iou_threshold: float = 0.5,
    class_names: Mapping[int, str] | None = None,
    save_images: bool = True,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Evaluate predictions against ground truth and write a full report.

    The Python equivalent of the ``hires evaluate`` command. The following
    is written to ``output_dir``:

    ``detection_report.csv``
        Per-class metrics; see :func:`detection_report`.
    ``confusion_matrix.csv``, ``confusion_matrix.png``
        See :func:`confusion_matrix`.
    ``precision_recall.csv``, ``precision_recall.png``
        See :func:`precision_recall_curve`.
    ``matches.csv``
        One row per match with the traits of both objects; see
        :meth:`MatchResult.to_frame`.
    ``comparisons/{name}.png``
        The matches drawn on each image (``save_images``), for collections
        whose image is known; see :func:`hires.plot.comparison`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    gt, pred : Collection or Album
        Ground truth and predictions; see :func:`match`. Collections present
        in only one album are skipped with a logged warning.
    output_dir : path-like
        Directory for all outputs; created if needed.
    iou_threshold : float, default 0.5
        Minimum IoU for two polygons to be matched.
    class_names : mapping of int to str, optional
        ``{class_id: label}`` used in the tables and figures.
    save_images : bool, default True
        Write the comparison images.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        The detection report.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If two albums have no collection in common.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> gt = hires.read_album("labels/", image_dir="images/")  # doctest: +SKIP
    >>> pred = hires.read_album("results/", image_dir="images/")  # doctest: +SKIP
    >>> report = hires.evaluate(gt, pred, "evaluation/")  # doctest: +SKIP
    >>> report.loc["all", ["precision", "recall", "f1"]]  # doctest: +SKIP
    """
    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

    from . import plot

    iou_threshold = _check_threshold(iou_threshold)
    pairings, gt_only, pred_only = _pair_inputs(gt, pred)
    if not pairings:
        raise ValueError("gt and pred have no collection in common; nothing to evaluate.")
    for side, names in (("ground truth", gt_only), ("predictions", pred_only)):
        if names:
            logger.warning(
                "Skipped %d collection(s) found only in the %s: %s%s",
                len(names),
                side,
                ", ".join(names[:10]),
                ", ..." if len(names) > 10 else "",
            )

    result = _match_pairings(pairings, iou_threshold, False, gt_only, pred_only)
    report = _detection_report(pairings, iou_threshold, COCO_THRESHOLDS, class_names)
    matrix = _confusion_matrix(result, class_names, "background")
    curve = _precision_recall_curve(result, None)

    output_dir = Path(output_dir)
    output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    report.to_csv(output_dir / "detection_report.csv")
    matrix.to_csv(output_dir / "confusion_matrix.csv")
    curve.to_csv(output_dir / "precision_recall.csv", index=False)
    result.to_frame(class_names=class_names).to_csv(output_dir / "matches.csv", index=False)
    plt.close(plot.confusion_matrix(matrix, save=output_dir / "confusion_matrix.png").figure)
    plt.close(plot.precision_recall(curve, save=output_dir / "precision_recall.png").figure)

    if save_images:
        drawn = 0
        for pairing in pairings:
            image_path = pairing.gt.image_path or pairing.pred.image_path
            if image_path is None:
                continue
            plot.comparison(
                image_path,
                result.filter(lambda m, name=pairing.name: m.image == name),
                save=output_dir / "comparisons" / f"{pairing.name or 'image'}.png",
            )
            drawn += 1
        if drawn < len(pairings):
            logger.info(
                "Comparison images written for %d of %d collections; the others have "
                "no image_path.",
                drawn,
                len(pairings),
            )

    logger.info("Evaluation of %d collection(s) written to %s", len(pairings), output_dir)
    return report

def summary(self) -> dict[str, float]:
    """Return the overall counts, precision, recall, F1 and mean IoU.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        ``n_gt`` and ``n_pred`` (objects in the ground truth and in the
        predictions), the four status counts, ``precision``, ``recall``
        and ``f1`` (a misclassified pair counts against both; ``0.0`` when
        undefined), and ``mean_iou`` over the matched pairs (``nan``
        without any).

    See Also
    --------
    detection_report : The same metrics per class, with average precision.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> hires.metrics.match(gt, pred).summary()["f1"]  # doctest: +SKIP
    0.93
    """
    counts = self.counts()
    tp = counts["tp"]
    n_gt = tp + counts["misclassified"] + counts["fn"]
    n_pred = tp + counts["misclassified"] + counts["fp"]
    precision = tp / n_pred if n_pred else 0.0
    recall = tp / n_gt if n_gt else 0.0
    f1 = 2 * precision * recall / (precision + recall) if precision + recall else 0.0
    ious = [m.iou for m in self._matches if m.is_matched]
    return {
        "n_gt": n_gt,
        "n_pred": n_pred,
        **counts,
        "precision": precision,
        "recall": recall,
        "f1": f1,
        "mean_iou": float(np.mean(ious)) if ious else float("nan"),
    }

def pick(
    self,
    status: str = "tp",
    *,
    by: str = "median_iou",
    image: str | None = None,
    seed: int | None = None,
) -> Match:
    """Select one representative match with the given status.

    Parameters
    ----------
    status : str, default "tp"
        One of ``"tp"``, ``"misclassified"``, ``"fp"``, ``"fn"``.
    by : {"median_iou", "best_iou", "worst_iou", "random"}, default "median_iou"
        Which candidate to return: the one with the median, highest or
        lowest IoU, or a random one.
    image : str, optional
        Restrict the selection to one image (collection).
    seed : int, optional
        Seed for ``by="random"``.

    Returns
    -------
    Match

    Raises
    ------
    LookupError
        If there is no match with that status.

    See Also
    --------
    hires.plot.individual : Draw the selected match.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> typical = matches.pick("tp", image="C1-1_control")  # doctest: +SKIP
    >>> hires.plot.individual(typical, save="example.png")  # doctest: +SKIP
    """
    if status not in STATUSES:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown status {status!r}; choose from {STATUSES}.")
    choices = ("median_iou", "best_iou", "worst_iou", "random")
    if by not in choices:
        raise ValueError(f"by must be one of {choices}, got {by!r}.")

    pool = self._matches if image is None else self._in_image(image)
    candidates = [m for m in pool if m.status == status]
    if not candidates:
        raise LookupError(
            f"No match with status {status!r}" + (f" in image {image!r}." if image else ".")
        )
    if by == "random":
        return candidates[int(np.random.default_rng(seed).integers(len(candidates)))]
    ordered = sorted(candidates, key=lambda m: m.iou)
    if by == "best_iou":
        return ordered[-1]
    if by == "worst_iou":
        return ordered[0]
    return ordered[len(ordered) // 2]

def to_frame(
    self,
    *,
    traits: bool = True,
    class_names: Mapping[int, str] | None = None,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return one row per match as a ``pandas.DataFrame``.

    The row index is the position of the match in this result, so
    ``result[i]`` is the match described by row ``i``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    traits : bool, default True
        Add ``gt_{trait}`` and ``pred_{trait}`` columns for every trait in
        :data:`hires.TRAIT_NAMES`, measured with the image size and
        physical scale of each source collection.
    class_names : mapping of int to str, optional
        ``{class_id: label}``. Adds the columns ``gt_class_name`` and
        ``pred_class_name``.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        Columns ``image``, ``status``, ``iou``, ``class_match``,
        ``gt_index``, ``pred_index``, ``gt_class``, ``pred_class``,
        ``gt_confidence``, ``pred_confidence`` and, optionally, the class
        name and trait columns. Fields of a missing annotation are null.

    Examples
    --------
    List the individuals of one image, then look one of them up:

    >>> table = matches.for_image("C1-1_control").to_frame(  # doctest: +SKIP
    ...     traits=False, class_names={0: "D. pulex", 1: "D. galeata"}
    ... )
    >>> table[table["status"] == "misclassified"]  # doctest: +SKIP
    """
    import pandas as pd

    rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for m in self._matches:
        row: dict[str, Any] = {
            "image": m.image,
            "status": m.status,
            "iou": m.iou,
            "class_match": m.class_match,
            "gt_index": m.gt_index,
            "pred_index": m.pred_index,
            "gt_class": None if m.gt is None else m.gt.class_id,
            "pred_class": None if m.pred is None else m.pred.class_id,
            "gt_confidence": None if m.gt is None else m.gt.confidence,
            "pred_confidence": None if m.pred is None else m.pred.confidence,
        }
        if traits:
            gt_source, pred_source = self._sources.get(m.image, (None, None))
            row.update(_prefixed_traits("gt_", m.gt, gt_source))
            row.update(_prefixed_traits("pred_", m.pred, pred_source))
        rows.append(row)

    columns = [
        "image",
        "status",
        "iou",
        "class_match",
        "gt_index",
        "pred_index",
        "gt_class",
        "pred_class",
        "gt_confidence",
        "pred_confidence",
    ]
    if traits:
        columns += [f"gt_{t}" for t in TRAIT_NAMES] + [f"pred_{t}" for t in TRAIT_NAMES]

    frame = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=columns)
    for column in ("gt_index", "pred_index", "gt_class", "pred_class"):
        frame[column] = frame[column].astype("Int64")
    for column in columns[8:]:
        frame[column] = frame[column].astype(float)
    frame["class_match"] = frame["class_match"].astype(bool)
    if class_names is not None:
        for position, side in ((8, "pred"), (7, "gt")):
            labels = [
                None if pd.isna(c) else class_names.get(int(c), str(int(c)))
                for c in frame[f"{side}_class"]
            ]
            frame.insert(position, f"{side}_class_name", pd.Series(labels, dtype=object))
    return frame

def average_precision(
    gt: Collection | Album,
    pred: Collection | Album,
    *,
    iou_threshold: float = 0.5,
) -> pd.Series:
    """Average precision per class at one IoU threshold.

    Predictions of each class are ranked by confidence and the area under
    the interpolated precision-recall curve is returned. A prediction counts
    as correct when :func:`match` paired it with a ground-truth object of the
    same class.

    Parameters
    ----------
    gt, pred : Collection or Album
        Ground truth and predictions; see :func:`match`.
    iou_threshold : float, default 0.5
        Minimum IoU for two polygons to be matched.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.Series
        AP indexed by class id. Classes without ground truth or without
        predictions score ``0.0``.

    Notes
    -----
    Matching is greedy by IoU and independent of confidence, which differs
    slightly from the COCO protocol where predictions claim ground truth in
    confidence order. Predictions without a confidence are ranked last.
    """
    import pandas as pd

    iou_threshold = _check_threshold(iou_threshold)
    pairings, _, _ = _pair_inputs(gt, pred)
    result = _match_pairings(pairings, iou_threshold)
    values = _average_precision(result, _class_ids(result, None))
    return pd.Series(values, name=f"ap@{iou_threshold:g}", dtype=float).rename_axis("class_id")

def iou(a: Annotation | Polygon, b: Annotation | Polygon) -> float:
    """Intersection-over-union of two polygons.

    Parameters
    ----------
    a, b : Annotation or shapely.geometry.Polygon

    Returns
    -------
    float
        Value in ``[0, 1]``; ``0.0`` when the polygons do not overlap.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> from shapely.geometry import box
    >>> iou(box(0, 0, 2, 1), box(1, 0, 3, 1))
    0.3333333333333333
    """
    first, second = _polygon(a), _polygon(b)
    intersection = first.intersection(second).area
    if intersection == 0:
        return 0.0
    union = first.area + second.area - intersection
    return float(intersection / union) if union > 0 else 0.0

def iou_matrix(
    gt: Iterable[Annotation | Polygon],
    pred: Iterable[Annotation | Polygon],
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Pairwise polygon IoU between two sets of annotations.

    Parameters
    ----------
    gt, pred : iterable of Annotation or Polygon
        Typically two :class:`~hires.Collection` objects of the same image.

    Returns
    -------
    numpy.ndarray
        Array of shape ``(len(gt), len(pred))``; element ``[i, j]`` is the
        IoU of ``gt[i]`` and ``pred[j]``.
    """
    gt_polygons = np.array([_polygon(a) for a in gt], dtype=object)
    pred_polygons = np.array([_polygon(a) for a in pred], dtype=object)
    matrix = np.zeros((len(gt_polygons), len(pred_polygons)), dtype=float)
    if matrix.size == 0:
        return matrix

    tree = STRtree(pred_polygons)
    gt_index, pred_index = tree.query(gt_polygons, predicate="intersects")
    if gt_index.size == 0:
        return matrix

    left = gt_polygons[gt_index]
    right = pred_polygons[pred_index]
    intersection = shapely.area(shapely.intersection(left, right))
    union = shapely.area(left) + shapely.area(right) - intersection
    values = np.divide(
        intersection, union, out=np.zeros_like(intersection), where=union > 0
    )
    matrix[gt_index, pred_index] = values
    return matrix

def overlay(
    image: str | os.PathLike[str] | np.ndarray,
    annotations: Iterable[Annotation],
    *,
    class_names: Mapping[int, str] | None = None,
    fill: bool = True,
    boxes: bool = True,
    labels: bool = True,
    alpha: float = 0.5,
    save: str | os.PathLike[str] | None = None,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Draw annotations on top of their image.

    Parameters
    ----------
    image : path-like or numpy.ndarray
        Image file, or an 8-bit BGR array of shape ``(height, width, 3)``.
    annotations : iterable of Annotation
        Usually a :class:`~hires.Collection`.
    class_names : mapping of int to str, optional
        ``{class_id: label}`` for the text labels. Class ids are shown when
        omitted.
    fill : bool, default True
        Fill and outline the polygons.
    boxes : bool, default True
        Draw axis-aligned bounding boxes.
    labels : bool, default True
        Write ``"{index} {class} {confidence}"`` at each object.
    alpha : float, default 0.5
        Opacity of the drawing over the image.
    save : path-like, optional
        Write the result to this file (any format OpenCV supports).

    Returns
    -------
    numpy.ndarray
        RGB image of shape ``(height, width, 3)``.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> rgb = hires.plot.overlay("scan.tif", collection, save="annotated.png")  # doctest: +SKIP
    >>> plt.imshow(rgb)  # doctest: +SKIP
    """
    import cv2

    base = _load_bgr(image)
    height, width = base.shape[:2]
    canvas = base.copy()
    names = class_names or {}

    for index, ann in enumerate(annotations):
        red, green, blue = PALETTE[ann.class_id % len(PALETTE)]
        color = (blue, green, red)
        points = _pixel_points(ann, width, height)

        if fill:
            cv2.polylines(canvas, [points], True, (255, 255, 255), 4, cv2.LINE_AA)
            cv2.polylines(canvas, [points], True, (0, 0, 0), 2, cv2.LINE_AA)
            cv2.fillPoly(canvas, [points], color)
        if boxes:
            x0, y0 = points.min(axis=0)
            x1, y1 = points.max(axis=0)
            cv2.rectangle(canvas, (int(x0), int(y0)), (int(x1), int(y1)), color, 2)
        if labels:
            text = f"{index} {names.get(ann.class_id, ann.class_id)}"
            if ann.confidence is not None:
                text += f" {ann.confidence:.2f}"
            x, y = (int(v) for v in points.mean(axis=0))
            y = y - 10 if y > 20 else y + 20
            font = cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX
            cv2.putText(canvas, text, (x + 1, y + 1), font, 0.5, (0, 0, 0), 2, cv2.LINE_AA)
            cv2.putText(canvas, text, (x, y), font, 0.5, (255, 255, 255), 1, cv2.LINE_AA)

    blended = cv2.addWeighted(canvas, alpha, base, 1.0 - alpha, 0)
    return _finish_image(blended, save)

def comparison(
    image: str | os.PathLike[str] | np.ndarray,
    matches: MatchResult,
    *,
    alpha: float = 0.5,
    save: str | os.PathLike[str] | None = None,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Draw the outcome of matching predictions against ground truth.

    True positives and misclassifications are drawn with the predicted
    polygon, false positives with the prediction and false negatives with
    the missed ground-truth polygon, coloured by :data:`STATUS_COLORS`
    (green, orange, red, blue).

    Parameters
    ----------
    image : path-like or numpy.ndarray
        Image file, or an 8-bit BGR array.
    matches : MatchResult
        Result of :func:`hires.metrics.match` for this image. For an album
        result, select one image first:
        ``matches.filter(lambda m: m.image == "scan")``.
    alpha : float, default 0.5
        Opacity of the drawing over the image.
    save : path-like, optional
        Write the result to this file.

    Returns
    -------
    numpy.ndarray
        RGB image of shape ``(height, width, 3)``.
    """
    import cv2

    base = _load_bgr(image)
    height, width = base.shape[:2]
    canvas = base.copy()

    for m in matches:
        shown = m.pred if m.pred is not None else m.gt
        red, green, blue = STATUS_COLORS[m.status]
        points = _pixel_points(shown, width, height)
        cv2.fillPoly(canvas, [points], (blue, green, red))
        cv2.polylines(canvas, [points], True, (255, 255, 255), 2, cv2.LINE_AA)

    blended = cv2.addWeighted(canvas, alpha, base, 1.0 - alpha, 0)
    return _finish_image(blended, save)
